The Stewards deferred the declaration of weighed-in to establish the circumstances for PAKISTAN STAR failing to take any active part in the race from near the 1600 Metres.  After viewing the videos, it was established that no circumstances existed which would result in PAKISTAN STAR being removed from the field and accordingly weighed-in was declared on the numbers as semaphored by the Judge.  J Moreira stated that after assuming a position at the rear of the small field he had to ride his mount along in the early stages to ensure that it did not become detached from the field.  He said approaching the 1700 Metres he was required to commence riding the horse along vigorously as PAKISTAN STAR would not stretch out and appeared to him as though the horse was going to pull up.  He said when he commenced to ride the horse along, PAKISTAN STAR continued to give ground and he slapped the horse down the shoulder with the whip at about the 1650 Metres on a number of occasions.  He said, despite riding the horse vigorously, PAKISTAN STAR became unbalanced in its action and refused to race.  He said, despite this, he continued to ride PAKISTAN STAR aggressively passing the 1600 Metres, however, the more he rode the horse, the more it refused to race and passing the 1600 Metres was many lengths detached from the main body of the field.  He added near the 1550 Metres PAKISTAN STAR, despite him continuing to ride the horse along, pulled up of its own accord.  He said in an attempt to ensure that PAKISTAN STAR did not perform in the same manner in the future, he attempted to have the horse recommence galloping as he felt that this would be in the horseâs best interests in respect of its future racing.  He said it took a considerable amount of time and urging for PAKISTAN STAR to recommence galloping and even then was inclined to pull up on a number of occasions before stretching out properly.  The Stewards ruled that PAKISTAN STAR must barrier trial satisfactorily in a series of consecutive barrier trials and be subjected to an official veterinary examination before being allowed to race again.  The Stewards also ruled that at least one of these trials must be over 1600 Metres on the turf at Sha Tin.  A veterinary inspection of PAKISTAN STAR immediately following the race did not show any significant findings other that the horse was noted to have weal marks at its right flank and quarters.  In the circumstances, J Moreira was fined the sum of $10,000 for improper use of the whip.

A short distance later, LITTLE FANTASY was crowded for room between CLEVER SPIRIT and POLYMER LUCK (C Schofield) which shifted in.  C Schofield was advised that whilst there were some circumstances associated with this incident, namely both CLEVER SPIRIT and LITTLE FANTASY being badly unbalanced as a result of contact between those horses, nonetheless he was reprimanded and advised to ensure that he reacts more promptly to his mount shifting ground than he did on this occasion.  During this incident, LITTLE FANTASY lost its right hind plate.  SUNNY ORIENT, which was following LITTLE FANTASY and CLEVER SPIRIT, was hampered when held up for clear running in consequence.  TRENDY WIN, which was following SUNNY ORIENT, was shifted out away from the heels of that horse near the 300 Metres.  TRENDY WIN was then held up for clear running until passing the 250 Metres.
Passing the 250 Metres, TORNEY was bumped by DIAMOND LEGEND (S Clipperton) when racing tight inside that horse which shifted in under pressure.  Whilst DIAMOND LEGEND was inclined to lay in at this time, nonetheless S Clipperton was reprimanded and advised that he should have made a far greater effort than he did on this occasion to prevent his mount form shifting ground.
When questioned, C Schofield stated that it had been intended to lead on POLYMER LUCK if possible.  He said in accordance with his instructions he rode his mount positively in the early stages, however, POLYMER LUCK did not show as much early speed as he anticipated.  He said passing the winning post on the first occasion he was able to shift in to race outside the leader CLEVER SPIRIT and having regard to the amount of use he had made of POLYMER LUCK to get to this position, he did not believe it was reasonable to continue pushing his mount to cross CLEVER SPIRIT.  He said for this reason he elected to remain racing to the outside of that horse and he was able to obtain cover behind CAREFREE LET GO near the 1100 Metres and further into the race behind LITTLE FANTASY.  He added POLYMER LUCK travelled well behind the speed and then in the Straight finished off the race satisfactorily.
When questioned regarding the disappointing performance of CLEVER SPIRIT, J Moreira stated that his mount was very unsettled prior to the race which was in contrast to its last start when successful.  He said CLEVER SPIRIT travelled keenly to the Start and he had to walk the horse for some time before being loaded into the barriers so as to have it settle better.  He said after beginning well, he rode his mount along in the early stages to cross runners to his inside and he was able to obtain the rail passing the winning post on the first occasion.  He said CLEVER SPIRIT travelled comfortably in the early and middle stages, however, when crossed by CAREFREE LET GO near the 800 Metres, CLEVER SPIRIT immediately came off the bridle and he had to niggle at the horse in an endeavour to have it maintain its position.  He said CLEVER SPIRIT came under heavy pressure prior to the 400 Metres and after becoming unbalanced at the entrance to the Straight then gave ground noticeably over the concluding stages.  He added it was particularly concerning the manner in which CLEVER SPIRIT gave ground over the final 200 Metres.  Mr C Fownes, the trainer of CLEVER SPIRIT, stated that the horse had done well since its last start success and accordingly he expected it to race well.  He said CLEVER SPIRIT has some issues and for this reason he adopted a similar track work schedule to that prior to its last start success.  He said he was unable to offer any explanation for the horseâs disappointing performance at this time.  A veterinary inspection of CLEVER SPIRIT immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of CLEVER SPIRIT, a last start winner, was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, CLEVER SPIRIT will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
A veterinary inspection of TRENDY WIN and SUNNY ORIENT immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

OUR FOLKS lost its left front plate after the race.
When questioned, Z Purton stated that, from barrier 12, he had been asked to shift LUCKY TIME across behind runners in the early stages and then have the horse travel where it was comfortable.  He said after beginning satisfactorily, he steadied LUCKY TIME in accordance with his instructions and commenced to shift it across to obtain a position closer to the rail.  He said after shifting to the inside of GREAT TOPLIGHT approaching the 1000 Metres, he rode his mount along including slapping it down the shoulder with the whip in an endeavour to have it improve its position.  He said LUCKY TIME, which was racing for the first time, was reluctant to improve its position at this time and he had to continue niggling at the horse in an endeavour to encourage it to improve.  He said throughout the middle stages he continued to slap the horse down the shoulder in an attempt to make up ground to be racing closer behind GREAT TOPLIGHT.  He said when GREAT TOPLIGHT shifted out passing the 500 Metres, he immediately commenced to ride LUCKY TIME along to improve its position inside that horse.  He said however, due to its inexperience, LUCKY TIME was initially reluctant to improve its position, however, when GREAT TOPLIGHT shifted out further, LUCKY TIME appeared to gain more confidence and then commenced to finish off the race better.  He added he rode LUCKY TIME vigorously hands and heels in the early part of the Straight, however, the horse seemed reluctant to fully stretch out and it was not until near the 200 Metres that LUCKY TIME commenced to finish off the race with more purpose.  He added over the concluding stages, when closing off the race strongly, LUCKY TIME was unable to obtain clear running and consequently he was not able to ride the horse out to the end of the race due to be awkwardly placed close to the heels of AMAZING MOMENT.
After the race, B Prebble stated that FOREVER ACCURATE was not comfortable in its action over the latter stages of the race.  A veterinary inspection of FOREVER ACCURATE immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of FOREVER ACCURATE, which finished tailed out, was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, FOREVER ACCURATE will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
When questioned regarding the performance of MULTIGOGO, J Moreira stated that he had to ride his mount along hard in the early stages to obtain a forward position as instructed.  He said it was not until after the 900 Metres that he was able to improve his position sufficiently to cross ALL YOU NEED to his inside and race in a position one horse off the rail.  He said MULTIGOGO did not travel on the bit at any stage of the race and he had to niggle at the horse prior to the 600 Metres in an endeavour to have it maintain its position.  He said he rode MULTIGOGO vigorously rounding the Home Turn and in the early part of the Straight, however, the horse did not respond to his riding and ran disappointingly.  A veterinary inspection of MULTIGOGO immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of MULTIGOGO, which was favoured for todayâs race, was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, MULTIGOGO will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
MULTIGOGO, ALL YOU NEED and REGENCY DARLING were sent for sampling.
<3/7/2017  Additional Veterinary Report>FOREVER ACCURATE, which performed poorly, was examined by the Veterinary Officer who said at that time there were no significant findings.  FOREVER ACCURATE was again examined by the Veterinary Officer at the stables of Trainer A Lee this morning.  He said at this time he noted the horse to be lame in its left front leg and to have sustained a small cut to the front of the right hind fetlock.  As previously advised, FOREVER ACCURATE will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination before being allowed to race again.

CROWN AVENUE and SURE PEACE began only fairly.
WINASWEWISH shifted out at the start and bumped RUBY COAST.
GRAN MASTER and IMPERIAL CONCORDE bumped at the start.

Passing the 1600 Metres, WINASWEWISH was steadied away from the heels of BEST TANGO (Apprentice M F Poon) which, after initially shifting into the running of WINASWEWISH, was then taken in further by J Moreira (GRAN MASTER) which shifted in.  Apprentice Poon was reprimanded for initially shifting in and crowding WINASWEWISH whilst J Moreira was advised to exercise more care in respect of his contribution to this incident.
CLOUD NINE travelled wide and without cover until passing the 800 Metres at which time BEST TANGO was left racing wide and without cover.
After being crossed by CLOUD NINE passing the 700 Metres, BALAY BALAY momentarily shifted out away from the heels of that horse.  GRAN MASTER, which was following, improved of its own accord to be racing close to the heels of BALAY BALAY and in doing so struck the heels of that horse, became badly unbalanced and lost ground.  J Moreira stated that in this incident GRAN MASTER appeared to strike itself and he was concerned for a number of strides that the horse may have broken down.  He said a short distance after this he was able to establish that the horse had not gone amiss and therefore he continued to ride it out, however, GRAN MASTER finished off the race only one-paced.  A veterinary inspection of GRAN MASTER immediately following the race including an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse's trachea and also found the horse to be a "roarerâ.  Before being allowed to race again, GRAN MASTER will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
After the 600 Metres, BEST TANGO raced tight outside BALAY BALAY due to that horse shifting out to improve around CLOUD NINE.
Near the 150 Metres, SPICY KAKA was shifted away from the heels of BEST TANGO which, after initially being directed out by BALAY BALAY, then shifted out and away from that horse.
Passing the 150 Metres, HAPPY ROCKY was momentarily steadied when improving into tight running between NAMJONG INVINCIBLE and GRAN MASTER which shifted out.
Over the concluding stages, IMPERIAL CONCORDE was awkwardly placed outside SURE PEACE.
After the race, O Doleuze reported that NAMJONG INVINCIBLE seemed to him to race "flatâ.  A veterinary inspection of NAMJONG INVINCIBLE immediately following the race including an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse's trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, NAMJONG INVINCIBLE will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
When questioned regarding the disappointing performance of FOREVER POSH, Z Purton stated that, from an inside barrier, he was able to obtain a good position behind the leader FIVE STARS AGENT without having to make use of the horse.  He said whilst the tempo of the race at times were quicker than what he had hoped, FOREVER POSH was unable to maintain its position behind FIVE STARS AGENT when that horse quickened passing the 500 Metres.  He said he placed FOREVER POSH under heavy pressure, however, the horse did not quicken at any stage and over the concluding stages gave ground and finished at the rear of the field.  A veterinary inspection of FOREVER POSH immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
A veterinary inspection of RUBY COAST immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of RUBY COAST, which finished tailed out, was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, RUBY COAST will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
GRAN MASTER, CROWN AVENUE and FIVE STARS AGENT were sent for sampling.
<3/7/2017  Additional Veterinary Report>GRAN MASTER, which performed poorly, was examined by the Veterinary Officer who said at that time an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horseâs trachea and also found the horse to be a "roarerâ.  GRAN MASTER was again examined by the Veterinary Officer at the stables of Trainer L Ho this morning.  He said at this time he noted the horse to have sustained superficial wounds to the right front and both hind legs.  As previously advised, GRAN MASTER will be subjected to an official veterinary examination before being allowed to race again.

After weighing out to ride HANGâS DECISION in this race and whilst the horse was being saddled up, K C Leung took ill and consequently was not able to fulfil his riding engagement.  Due to the late nature of the indisposition and as no other rider was available to ride HANGâS DECISION at or near the horseâs allocated weight of 116 lbs, permission was granted for B Prebble to ride HANGâS DECISION 4 lbs overweight.  After initially being presented in the Parade Ring with K C Leungâs saddle, HANGâS DECISION was removed from the parade to facilitate the late re-saddling of the horse.

HEROIC GURU began only fairly.
CIRCUIT HASSLER and LIMITLESS bumped at the start.
From the outside barrier, HAPPY AGILITY was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
LIMITLESS travelled keenly after the 1100 Metres.
Throughout the race, ALMABABY travelled wide and without cover.
After the race, B Prebble was momentarily dislodged from HANGâS DECISION without incident.
When questioned, S Clipperton stated that as LUCKY GIRL was racing over 1400 Metres, it was felt that the horse may not have sufficient early speed to be racing with the leaders as it was anticipated that the race would be run at a strong tempo.  He said he was asked to begin positively on LUCKY GIRL if possible and then have the horse racing where it was comfortable.  He said LUCKY GIRL began only fairly and, as his mount was clearly out-paced in the early stages, he attempted to shift across behind runners and improve ground in an attempt to obtain a position in about midfield.  He said whilst todayâs race was run at a strong tempo which suited horses coming from towards the back of the field, nonetheless LUCKY GIRL finished off the race satisfactorily given the distance of the race and the fact that it was not able to lead todayâs race.
When questioned, Z Purton stated that in the early part of the Straight he shifted LIMITLESS to the inside of HANGâS DECISION as SAULâS SPECIAL, which was racing to the outside of that horse, was commencing to give ground.  He said at the 400 Metres clear running was available ahead of LIMITLESS, however, the horse commenced to hang in badly as it did at its most recent start.  He said however LIMITLESS hung in more severely today than it did at its last start and he had to apply heavy pressure to the outside rein to prevent the horse from continuing to hang in.  He said passing the 250 Metres he was able to change his whip over into his right hand and at this time he dropped his right rein.  He said because of the manner in which LIMITLESS was hanging in, he was not able to properly test the horse in the early part of the Straight.  He added after the 200 Metres whilst LIMITLESS was continuing to hang in, he was able to direct that horse to the outside of MY DARLING.  He said LIMITLESS then continued to hang in under pressure and proved difficult to ride and it was not until the concluding stages that LIMITLESS improved to be racing directly to the outside of MY DARLING and then commenced to race more tractably.  The racing manners of LIMITLESS were considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, LIMITLESS will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial.
When questioned, Apprentice M F Poon stated that he had been asked to ride LINE SEEKER in a forward position from its inside barrier and obtain a position behind the leaders if possible.  He said he was also told that as LINE SEEKER has well-documented breathing problems, he should not unnecessarily restrain the horse.  He said in accordance with his instructions he rode his mount along in the early stages to establish a forward position and LINE SEEKER then travelled keenly.  He said having in mind that he was asked not to restrain LINE SEEKER too heavily, he attempted to steady the tempo on the horse with a view to allowing runners to his outside to cross LINE SEEKER.  He said however when those horses remained racing outside LINE SEEKER, this resulted in LINE SEEKER having to lead the race and travelling too keenly.  He said for this reason LINE SEEKER was then not able to finish off the race.  A veterinary inspection of LINE SEEKER immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Following the race, SAULâS SPECIAL was noted to have a small quantity of blood at the left nostril due to an abrasion.  An endoscopic examination of SAULâS SPECIAL deemed that horse not to have bled.  The performance of SAULâS SPECIAL, which finished tailed out, was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, SAULâS SPECIAL will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination. 
A veterinary inspection of THE GOLDEN AGE immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
MY DARLING, HANGâS DECISION and CIRCUIT HASSLER were sent for sampling.

TRAVEL FIRST was withdrawn on 30.6.17 by order of the Stewards acting on veterinary advice (lame right hind).  Before being allowed to race again, TRAVEL FIRST will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
GOLDEN SUN began only fairly.
From the outside barriers, UNICRON JEWELLERY and ENORMOUS HONOUR were shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
When being steadied to obtain cover passing the winning post on the first occasion, WHITE MAGIC travelled keenly and got its head up on a number of occasions.
Passing the 300 Metres, GONNA RUN and ENORMOUS HONOUR raced tight due to GOLDEN SUN shifting in.  Then near the 250 Metres, ENORMOUS HONOUR was steadied and shifted out away from the heels of WHO DAT SINGA which was giving ground.
For the majority of the race, MARQULA travelled wide and without cover and in the Straight gave ground. He added the only explanation he could offer for the horseâs disappointing performance was that it may not have handled the All Weather surface at its first time of asking under race conditions.  A veterinary inspection of UNICRON JEWELLERY immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
TURIN PEARL and WHITE MAGIC were sent for sampling.

Despite being hard ridden in the early stages, CHEERFUL BOY failed to muster speed and then passing the 900 Metres was left racing wide and without cover.

Approaching the 700 Metres, INDIGENOUS UNION got its head on the side and lay out when awkwardly placed behind HARD BALL GET.

The performance of WHAT MAN HORSE, which finished tailed out, was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, WHAT MAN HORSE will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

He said after taking up a forward position from a wide barrier, SAMâS LOVE travelled well in the middle stages, however, came under pressure rounding the Home Turn and then did not finish off the race. SAMâS LOVE, HARD BALL GET and AMAZING were sent for sampling.

Whilst in the saddling stalls, ELEGANCE PROMISE had its right front plate refitted.  ELEGANCE PROMISE was examined by the Veterinary Officer who said in his opinion it was suitable to race.
FANTASTIC SHOW began only fairly.

Approaching the 600 Metres, LUCKY STRYKER was awkwardly placed close to the heels of LUCKY MASTER.

ELEGANCE PROMISE and TELECOM SUN bumped near the 150 Metres.
Over the concluding stages, STRATHSPEY raced tight inside BINGO which shifted in after being awkwardly placed inside GALLANT RETURN.
